p2_b0.ocr: The table presents an analysis of bile salts across various animals, detailing specific bile salts associated with each species. The header "Animal" indicates the type of animal, while the header "Bile salts" specifies the corresponding bile salts.

p2_b1.ocr: The bear is associated with bile salts TUDC, TC, TDC, and TCDC. In contrast, the dog possesses bile salts TC, TCDC, and TDC. The cattle exhibit a wider variety, including TC, TDC, TCDC, TLC, GC, GDC, GCDC, GLC, and AC.

p2_b2.ocr:
Animal Bile salts
Bear TUDC, TC, TDC, TCDC
Dog TC, TCDC, TDC
Cattle TC, TDC, TCDC, TLC, GC, GDC, GCDC, GLC, AC
Pig TC, TDC, TCDC, THC, THDC, GC, GDC, GCDC, GHC, GHDC, GHOC
Snake TPC, TC, TDC
Rabbit GDC, TC, TDC, TCDC
Chicken TC, TCDC, TAC
Fish TCDC, TC, TDC, AC
Goose TCDC, TPHC, TBC
Duck TCDC, TPHC, TBC
Mouse TC, TDC, TCDC, T-β-MC, T-ω-MC, TUDC

p2_b3.ocr: The pig has a diverse range as well, with TC, TDC, TCDC, THC, THDC, GC, GDC, GCDC, GHC, GHDC, and GHOC. The snake is noted for having bile salts TPC, TC, and TDC, while the rabbit includes GDC, TC, TDC, and TCDC. The chicken is identified with TC, TCDC, and TAC, whereas the fish has TCDC, TC, TDC, and AC. The goose contains TCDC, TPHC, and TBC, and similarly, the duck features TCDC, TPHC, and TBC.

p2_b4.ocr: Finally, the mouse is detailed with bile salts TC, TDC, TCDC, T-β-MC, T-ω-MC, and TUDC. Each row reflects the unique combination of bile salts present in these animals, emphasizing the diversity in bile salt composition across species, with the cattle and pig showcasing the most extensive variety. The information underscores the biochemical complexity and evolutionary adaptations of these animals concerning their digestive processes.
